topic:
ANCHOR_PHRASE: Locally minimax prediction-risk certificates for continuous synthetic-control predictor tuning across active donor faces.

ACADEMIC_FIELD: Causal panel prediction and synthetic-control inference

MODE: gap

CLUSTER: panel

AXIS: (g)

MOTIF: M5+M8

TARGET_TIER: field

FIELD_CONTRACT: Derive an observable counterfactual prediction-risk graph and honest all-predictor confidence bands, and solve its local Gaussian confidence-band decision problem across active donor-face changes. A KKT rewrite, pointwise constrained-weight confidence set, generic conservative moment projection, or corrected causal-ATT CLT alone is below field. The hard contribution must quantify the optimal simultaneous risk-certificate cost through moving constraints, with an implementable computation and attaining procedures on specified local experiments. No compulsory positive kink penalty is asserted. Unknown rank, growing dimensions, arbitrary singleton-date summaries, post-factor drift within the specified block, and optimal inference for corrected causal ATT are out of scope.

BACKGROUND: Fry 2024 Lemma 1 and Propositions 1-3 use instrument/control moment limits and identify predictor weighting as an open practical choice. Fry's current Orthogonalized Synthetic Controls (June 26 2026), Lemma 2.1 and Proposition 4.1, removes constrained-nuisance effects from a corrected causal ATT; this candidate targets uncorrected prediction MSE instead. Canen-Song Simple Inference on a Simplex-Valued Weight (January 2026), Section 2.5 and Theorem 3.1, gives uniform joint inference for a fixed constrained optimizer and its functional via KKT cone projections. It does not provide simultaneous inference over continuously changing predictor objectives or solve the risk-graph local band decision problem. These primary results were read directly.

MODEL_REGIME: Observe one target and J fixed donors for n=T0 pre periods and the J untreated donors for T1 post periods, T1/n converging to a fixed positive finite ratio. Target post outcomes may be observed as treated but are not used to estimate the prediction-risk target. Fixed known rank r and fixed number L>=r of known contiguous pre blocks, each of length n_l with n_l/n bounded above and below and converging. Untreated means are constant within each block: Y_it(0)=f_l' mu_i+epsilon_it in pre block l and Y_it(0)=f_post' mu_i+epsilon_it in the single stable post block. All factor/loadings are fixed and bounded. Let A be the L-by-J donor pre-block mean matrix, a0 the target pre-block mean vector, and d the J-vector of post donor means. Require rank A=r, its r nonzero singular values in [c,C], a0 in col(A), and d in row(A); the target post mean is c0=d'A^+a0 under the common loading model. All constants are fixed uniformly. The stationary error vector epsilon_t in R^(J+1) has mean zero, uniformly bounded sub-Gaussian norm, contemporaneous covariance Sigma with eigenvalues in [c,C], and beta(k)<=C exp(-c k). The long-run covariance of phi_t=(epsilon_t,vech(epsilon_t epsilon_t'-Sigma)) has eigenvalues in [c,C]. This is a uniform condition; serial/cross-unit correlation is allowed. Predictors are X=S A and x=S a0 for a known fixed K-by-L matrix S of bounded norm: every original-date coefficient is S_kl/n_l, explicitly diffuse. rho>0 is fixed. For v in Delta_K, w_P(v) uniquely minimizes (x-Xw)'diag(v)(x-Xw)+rho||w||^2 over Delta_J. A future independent copy of the stationary post-regime outcome vector has mean (c0,d')' and error covariance Sigma. The target is its unconditional counterfactual prediction MSE R_P(v)=E[(Y_0,new(0)-w_P(v)'Y_D,new(0))^2]=[c0-d'w_P(v)]^2+(1,-w_P(v)')Sigma(1,-w_P(v)')'. This is a prediction-risk functional of the observed law, not corrected ATT. Define the graph G_P={(v,R_P(v)):v in Delta_K}.

LIVE_OPPORTUNITY: Replace a tuned predictor vector and a pointwise fit diagnostic with a same-panel confidence certificate for the entire counterfactual prediction-risk graph. The local question is the optimal simultaneous band length when predictor perturbations and moment noise move donor active faces on the same root-n scale.

GROUNDING: The prior presolve derived c0=d'A^+a0, rational support-wise KKT formulas, a uniform ridge perturbation bound, and the exact identity sqrt(n)(w_hat-w)=argmin over {h:1'h=0,h_j>=-sqrt(n)w_j} of 0.5h'H_hat h+[sqrt(n)(H_hat-H)w-sqrt(n)(f_hat-f)+sqrt(n)s]'h, where H=2(X'diag(v)X+rho I), f=2X'diag(v)x and s is the nonnegative KKT slack. This retains local slack and weight drift. A pointwise fixed-cone delta expansion fails in sup norm when the boundary moves. The new model removes the presolve's finite-information singleton-date counterexample and supplies residual-based covariance estimation because block means are constant.

KERNEL: K1: Characterize the complete semialgebraic KKT stratification of v->w(v) and its observable risk graph. Derive from the specified block/mixing primitives a joint same-panel moment expansion and construct measurable interval bands C_n(v) satisfying liminf_n inf_P P{R_P(v) in C_n(v) for every v in Delta_K}>=1-alpha and uniformly root-n stochastic maximum diameter, including distributions and selectors within O(n^-1/2) of any KKT face change. Thus any measurable v_hat inherits coverage for R_P(v_hat). Include all pre-weight estimation and covariance terms; fixed-weight post error variance is not the estimator variance. K2, the field-level hard theorem: determine and compute the following local decision value, rather than assuming a positive inflation formula. At a fixed interior signal/noise parameter theta0 of the rank-r mean model, let xi be any smooth identifiable local chart for theta=(A,a0,d,Sigma), with xi(theta0)=0. Restrict this local experiment to iid Gaussian errors, with fixed known block proportions, so it has Fisher information I(theta0) for xi from the actually observed panel. Choose v0 in Delta_K, M>0 and L0>0. Local alternatives are xi(theta_n(u))=u/sqrt(n), ||u||<=M; local predictor queries are v_n(t)=v0+t/sqrt(n), t in D={t:1't=0,t_j>=0 if v0_j=0,||t||<=L0}. Define Psi_theta0(u,t)=lim_n sqrt(n)[R_theta_n(u)(v_n(t))-R_theta0(v0)], derived using the shifted KKT QP. In the Gaussian experiment Z~N(u,I(theta0)^-1), allow randomized measurable bands C(Z,t) with interval sections and simultaneous coverage inf_{||u||<=M} P_u{Psi(u,t) in C(Z,t) for all t in D}>=1-alpha. Define L_alpha(theta0,v0;M,L0)=inf_C sup_{||u||<=M} E_u[sup_{t in D}diam C(Z,t)]. Derive a constructive characterization of this value from the active-face geometry, with certified finite-dimensional upper/lower approximations converging to it, and construct asymptotically attaining confidence bands on these specified Gaussian local neighborhoods. Prove the matching local asymptotic lower bound for panel procedures using the same observed-data experiment. K1's global mixing-class band and K2's local-optimal neighborhood bands may be different procedures. Quantify separated-face versus boundary costs under this single comparison criterion; the cost difference may be zero. A generic lower bound stated only as the defining infimum, or a conservative projection without solving this decision problem, does not deliver K2.

FOCAL_OBJECT: The observable counterfactual prediction-risk graph and the local minimax simultaneous-band length L_alpha(theta0,v0;M,L0).

COMPUTATION: Enumerate nonempty donor supports and KKT sign strata. For K1 use joint block-moment confidence regions and exact perturbed-QP inversion as a conservative benchmark, improving calibration through local drift. For K2 use finite KKT cells with truncated Gaussian integration and finite discretizations of parameter/query/observation spaces to produce certified converging upper and lower decision bounds; the proof must control discretization and Gaussian tail error, not simply posit an optimization oracle.

ESTIMATION_RUNG: Block sample means, rank-r completion based on their identified chart, pre-block-demeaned residual second moments, and a block/HAC estimate of their joint long-run covariance; simultaneous risk certificates valid after unsplit predictor tuning. Local Gaussian information and optimal confidence-band decision analysis on the stated iid submodels.

CONSUMER: Synth predictor weighting and its post-counterfactual validation workflow; mlsynth.SparseSC's L1 predictor search and California Proposition 99 replication. The result supplies risk confidence certificates for alternative predictor weights before choosing a synthetic predictor. Current Synth documentation lists built-in parametric/split-conformal inference, but those are outcome/ATT prediction intervals rather than all-predictor confidence bands for population prediction MSE. The theorem applies when the user's block-stable mean model is substantively appropriate; it is not a general guarantee for arbitrary macroeconomic trends.

MODE_LINES: Not applicable (gap mode).

MINIMAL_INSTANCE: r=2, J=3, K=L=2, equal-size pre blocks with factors e1 and e2, post factor (1,0), donor loadings (0,0),(1,0),(0,1), target loading (3/2,3/2), S=I, rho=1/20. Independent Gaussian errors have covariance diag(1,1,4,1) in target/donor order, satisfying all uniform mixing and moment-covariance conditions. A has rank2 and singular values1. The globally verified solution is w=(0,t,1-t), t=clip((40v-9)/22,0,1), where v=(v,1-v). Its risk is R(t)=17/4-5t+6t^2. At upper transition v0=31/40, R'(1)=7 is nonzero. Multiplying the first pre-block factor by a=1+u/sqrt(n) is a legal parameter perturbation; the upper KKT boundary moves with derivative -31/80, and the unclipped weight derivative in a is31/44. In this one-dimensional Gaussian subfamily with all other parameters fixed, root-n information for u is5/4, and the local risk curve is Psi(u,t)=7 min((20/11)t+(31/44)u,0) for the scalar predictor displacement t. This witnesses a nonconstant local confidence decision problem, not an asserted universal positive width penalty. Higher-dimensional local charts are required by K2, which is not limited to this subfamily.

PRIOR_ART: Fry2024 primary https://josephpatrickfry.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/a_method_of_moments_approach_to_asymptotically_unbiased_synthetic_controls-12.pdf; Fry2026 https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.00307; Canen-Song2026 https://arxiv.org/html/2501.15692v2. Additional direct checks: Vives-i-Bastida https://arxiv.org/pdf/2203.11576 gives predictor support, Choi-Kwon-Liao https://arxiv.org/html/2307.16370 needs growing cross-section for its no-split low-rank theory, and Koo-Guo August2026 https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02632 targets weight-robust effects rather than predictor risk. Generic comparison: Fang-Santos directionally differentiable inference and existing optimal uniform confidence-band theory; the proposed novelty is the solved moving-KKT risk-graph decision problem, not directional inference itself. Current exact-pair/citing searches found no exact match. Known queue/claims/bank checks found no predictor-risk qid match. This materially revises panel_predictor_face_inference, whose draft is internal/presolve_drafts/panel_predictor_face_inference.md; it must not be treated as an independent duplicate launch.

EST_ACHIEVABLE_TIER: field

CEILING_REASON: A full solution would combine a feasible causal counterfactual-risk object with a computed optimal simultaneous confidence decision through moving donor constraints. The field tier depends on the decision characterization and matching achievable bound; block-mean completion and generic QP projection alone are subfield.

LIKELY_DEATH: The local band value may reduce to an existing generic optimal confidence-band theorem with no panel-specific advance; all-v local attainment may require extra regularity not stated; or the computation may remain an unimplemented infimum rather than a constructive characterization.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The fresh presolver derived the local critical-cone risk map Psi(u,t)=a(u)+g' h(u,t), with h solving a fixed-Hessian critical-cone quadratic program, and finite SOCP formulas for curve distances. It derived finite acceptance-subset primal/dual programs plus explicit coverage, observation-grid, and parameter-net error bounds. In the moving-hinge witness the graph problem reduces to capped scalar Gaussian-mean inference; a separately formulated LP reproduced the binary minimax value 3.2098273958452164 to numerical precision. Checks covered multiple weak faces, strict-slack vertices, zero derivatives, predictor-simplex boundaries, saturation, chart dependence, missing target post outcomes, and covariance information; no source collision was found.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that the actual Gaussian panel's compact-local minimax band cost equals the certified finite-program limit for unrestricted randomized measurable bands, with experiment convergence preserving simultaneous coverage and expected maximum width.
EARLY KILL TEST: Solve the smallest local experiment containing both a weak-donor mean direction and a covariance-risk direction, bracket it with two nested certified programs, and verify uniform Gaussian/Wishart coverage transfer; pivot if required information or vanishing padding fails.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_predictor_risk_band_minimax.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct an honest root-n simultaneous confidence band for the unconditional counterfactual prediction-MSE graph over the full predictor simplex that remains uniformly valid when local moment perturbations change the active donor face?

source_refs.claim: Predictor choice and weighting are central to synthetic-control performance, and their theory and best practice remain open.
source_refs.author: Jaume Vives-i-Bastida

source_refs.claim: Synthetic-control weights converge toward minimizers of mean squared prediction risk, but no confidence band is given for risk indexed by predictor weights.
source_refs.author: Xiaomeng Zhang, Wendun Wang, Xinyu Zhang

source_refs.claim: Uniform KKT-cone inference is developed for a simplex optimizer and its functional at a fixed population objective, not a continuum of changing objectives.
source_refs.author: Nathan Canen, Kyungchul Song

source_refs.claim: The paper covers a future synthetic-control counterfactual, not population prediction MSE indexed by predictor tuning.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Yingjie Feng, Rocio Titiunik
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: Develop an extension with estimated covariance and prove stability of the chosen nested-support weights and coverage.
The note proves a fixed-dimensional face-envelope coverage theorem and oracle equivalence on separated faces.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing synthetic-control work either characterizes a limiting risk-minimizing weight, covers a future outcome, or performs inference for one fixed constrained objective. The closest prior CausalSmith constructions additionally assume deterministic weights or known covariance and handle only finitely many branches. A continuously indexed risk graph instead requires a joint moment-and-optimizer process in which estimated covariance, KKT slack, donor-weight drift, and predictor-query drift all enter at first order. At a face transition the critical cone itself moves, so neither pointwise fixed-cone delta inference nor a routine supremum bootstrap establishes uniform coverage.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would provide an observable estimator of the full risk graph, a uniform shifted-KKT expansion or exact inversion over the predictor simplex, and measurable interval sections with uniform simultaneous coverage and root-n maximum diameter, including root-n neighborhoods of every donor-face transition.

writing_exemplar.why: Its introduction directly motivates predictor weighting through counterfactual performance and interpretability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Synthetic controls require analyst-chosen predictor importance -> predictor weighting changes post-treatment performance and interpretation -> users need uncertainty for the entire population-risk graph before selecting a weighting

method_exemplars.technique: Represent simplex optimality by KKT residuals, project a Gaussian score onto the relevant polyhedral cone, and invert the adaptive statistic for uniform coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each donor weight is a simplex-constrained optimizer; the required advance couples the cone projections over a continuum while allowing their cones to move.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the directional derivative within a derivative-aware resampling scheme whose proof avoids the inconsistent ordinary bootstrap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The active-face QP map is directionally but not fully differentiable, although a moving-cone uniform derivative must replace the fixed-map derivative.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose synthetic-control uncertainty into estimated-weight and post-regime components and propagate both through simulation-based probability bounds under temporal dependence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired MSE band must retain both pre-weight and post-regime covariance uncertainty, but for an unconditional risk functional uniformly indexed by predictor weights.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the minimax worst-case expected maximum interval width for simultaneous bands on a finite piecewise-affine KKT risk curve in its compact Gaussian shift experiment, and can that value be computed by certified finite programs and transferred sharply to the observed synthetic-control panel experiment?

source_refs.claim: Bayes-minimax duality characterizes minimum worst-case expected-measure confidence sets for restricted location parameters.
source_refs.author: Steven N. Evans, Ben B. Hansen, Philip B. Stark

source_refs.claim: Finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds are derived for scalar linear functionals over convex Gaussian regression classes.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

source_refs.claim: KKT inversion yields valid confidence sets for a fixed noisy optimizer, but projection can over-cover and does not solve an expected-width band decision.
source_refs.author: Yu-Wei Hsieh, Xiaoxia Shi, Matthew Shum

source_refs.claim: Directional-delta resampling addresses local size for nonsmooth functionals but does not characterize minimax expected band width.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang, Andres Santos

source_refs.excerpt: Make the raw-to-local-Gaussian coverage-transfer lemma the next focal target, with explicit anti-concentration.
The all-strata measurable attainment claim remains an explicit open question.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest optimal-inference results treat scalar linear functionals or one-dimensional restricted location parameters, while KKT-inference papers cover one fixed optimizer and may over-cover through nuisance projection. Prior CausalSmith work computed only a deterministic conditional cutoff and left measurable attainment and raw-to-Gaussian coverage transfer open. Here the action is an interval-valued function over a continuum, coverage is uniform over a compact multivariate Gaussian mean set, and loss is the supremum of section widths. Solving it requires both density of certified finite rules in the unrestricted randomized decision class and a Le Cam transfer that preserves simultaneous coverage and an unbounded expected-width loss.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would prove a primal-dual or least-favorable-prior characterization of the Gaussian-band value, give certified finite upper and lower programs with explicit mesh and tail errors converging to it, construct attaining bands, and establish matching local asymptotic lower-bound and achievability transfers for panel procedures.

writing_exemplar.why: It turns honesty into a decision problem, derives a sharp efficiency benchmark, and continues through to computable procedures.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Honest coverage leaves many admissible procedures -> expected length supplies a comparison criterion -> solve the Gaussian decision problem and sharp efficiency bound -> extend the optimality program to simultaneous kinked KKT risk curves

method_exemplars.technique: Convert minimum worst-case expected confidence-set size into testing and Bayes-minimax dual problems, using finite-support least-favorable distributions to certify bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target also optimizes expected size over randomized measurable confidence procedures, replacing scalar set measure with the maximum width of interval sections.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode QP optimality using primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity, then invert moment conditions while profiling slack and multiplier nuisances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite KKT strata give the natural finite description of the risk curve and its acceptance regions, although optimality requires replacing conservative projection with a solved decision rule.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian convex-class geometry and modulus calculations to derive finite-sample confidence procedures and sharp expected-length efficiency bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the proof architecture for equality between a Gaussian decision value and an attainable procedure; the missing extension is from a scalar functional to a simultaneous piecewise-affine curve.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a same-panel selector that chooses predictor weights by minimizing an upper confidence envelope of counterfactual prediction risk receive an honest post-tuning risk certificate and a local oracle-regret limit uniformly across donor-face changes, without sample splitting?

source_refs.claim: Estimable information criteria select the predictor weighting matrix or regularization parameter as alternatives to cross-validation.
source_refs.author: Guillaume Allaire Pouliot, Zhen Xie, Ziyi Liu
source_refs.venue: arXiv working paper; revise-and-resubmit at Quantitative Economics

source_refs.claim: Searching a continuum of tuning choices invalidates pointwise intervals; adjusted critical values restore simultaneous validity over the searched range.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

source_refs.claim: Gaussian anti-concentration supports honest uniform bands with data-driven resolution choices once an appropriate process approximation is available.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Kengo Kato

source_refs.claim: The paper covers a fixed simplex optimizer and its functional, not selection after examining a continuum of predictor objectives.
source_refs.author: Nathan Canen, Kyungchul Song

open_problems.why_unsolved: Synthetic-control information criteria and cross-validation choose a tuning point but do not attach an honest population-risk certificate to the selected point. Bandwidth-snooping theory explains why pointwise inference is inadequate after a continuum search, but its indexed estimators lack the locally moving active-set geometry present here. At a weak donor face, both the estimated envelope and its argmin acquire local hinge terms. The missing proof step is therefore a joint epigraphical limit for the risk envelope and selected minimizer under local KKT slack, coupled to simultaneous coverage rather than an independent validation sample.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would define an implementable upper-envelope selector, prove that its reported interval covers its selected population risk uniformly without splitting, and derive a uniform local limit or sharp root-n regret bound that permits root-n donor-face transitions.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames predictor-weight selection as a practical out-of-sample-risk problem and provides an implementable alternative to unstable cross-validation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Predictor weighting controls model flexibility -> short pre-periods make cross-validation unreliable -> full-sample criteria enable tuning -> tuning still needs an honest risk certificate and regret guarantee after the search

method_exemplars.technique: Replace pointwise critical values with a Gaussian-supremum quantile over the complete searched range and prove validity for any reported data-dependent tuning choice.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems require inference surviving continuous unsplit tuning; the extension replaces a smooth Gaussian index process with a locally kinked KKT risk process.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine Gaussian-process coupling, supremum anti-concentration, and multiplier-bootstrap quantiles to prove honest uniform coverage under data-driven tuning.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This machinery can calibrate the risk envelope once a uniform moving-face Gaussian approximation is established.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the directional derivative and resample the nonsmooth first-order map instead of applying the ordinary bootstrap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The post-tuning argmin and active-face weight map are nested directionally differentiable operations whose joint local law determines oracle regret.

open_problems.open_problem: Can sparse synthetic-control predictor selection be equipped with a simultaneous population-risk surface band over its penalty path that remains honest when predictor-support and donor-active-face changes occur on the same root-n scale?

source_refs.claim: Sparse synthetic control develops predictor-selection theory and improved MSE rates but not uniform risk inference over the penalty path.
source_refs.author: Jaume Vives-i-Bastida

source_refs.claim: Active-set degrees of freedom support information criteria for SCM penalties and predictor weights, but uncertainty for selected population risk is not developed.
source_refs.author: Guillaume Allaire Pouliot, Zhen Xie, Ziyi Liu
source_refs.venue: arXiv working paper; revise-and-resubmit at Quantitative Economics

source_refs.claim: Constrained M-estimator limits are governed by projection onto tangent cones at a fixed true constraint geometry.
source_refs.author: Charles J. Geyer

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing work separately studies useful-predictor recovery and active-set risk estimation, but does not propagate uncertainty over the entire sparse tuning path. The source construction for continuous predictor weighting has finitely many rational KKT formulas indexed by donor support. Adding an L1-type predictor-selection penalty changes the first proof step: the stratification must index the product of predictor-support signs and donor-complementarity states, with two independently weak inequalities able to switch jointly. Searches combining sparse predictor selection, donor active sets, prediction-risk surfaces, and confidence bands found the selection papers but no occupied target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would characterize the joint predictor-support and donor-face stratification, construct a simultaneous band for population MSE indexed by the sparse penalty and retained predictor weights, and prove coverage and a limit law for a criterion- or envelope-selected sparse specification.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the closest destination framing: nuisance predictors can damage counterfactual quality while useful predictors should be selected transparently.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Synthetic-control performance depends on predictor content -> sparse selection can remove nuisance predictors and improve MSE -> users tune a sparsity penalty -> they need risk uncertainty along the full path where predictor and donor supports switch

method_exemplars.technique: Condition on active sets, rewrite the synthetic-control fit as equality-constrained least squares, and apply Stein-divergence calculations to estimate prediction risk.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its active-set risk calculation is the natural center of each stratum; uniform band theory must additionally handle neighborhoods where active sets change.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert adaptive polyhedral-cone projection statistics for simplex-constrained weights without assuming an interior solution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each donor-face component of the sparse path is a simplex problem, while predictor selection adds a second complementarity system.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish and estimate a composite directional derivative and use derivative-aware resampling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Joint predictor and donor support changes create a composition of nonsmooth maps for which ordinary bootstrap validity fails.

literature_map:
Vives-i-Bastida (2022) makes predictor selection and weighting a central unresolved synthetic-control design problem.
Zhang, Wang, and Zhang (2022) connect synthetic-control weights to limiting prediction-risk minimization but do not infer the indexed risk graph.
Canen and Song (2026) provide uniform cone-projection inference for one simplex optimizer and functional, leaving continuously changing objectives untreated.
Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) separate fitted-weight and post-period uncertainty for future-outcome prediction rather than population MSE.
Fry (2024) supplies fixed-donor moment limits under mixing that can support a joint block-moment expansion.
Fry (2026) orthogonalizes constrained-weight effects for corrected ATT, whereas prediction MSE must retain those first-order effects.
Pouliot, Xie, and Liu (2026) develop active-set degrees of freedom and information criteria for predictor and penalty selection without post-selection risk bands.
Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, ReStud) show why continuum tuning invalidates pointwise inference and how simultaneous calibration restores validity in smooth settings.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014) provide Gaussian coupling and anti-concentration tools once a suitable moving-face process approximation exists.
Fang and Santos (2019) handle directionally differentiable maps, but not a query-indexed map whose critical cone itself moves locally.
Hsieh, Shi, and Shum (2022) invert KKT systems for fixed noisy optimization problems while acknowledging projection conservatism.
Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005) characterize minimum expected-size confidence sets using Bayes-minimax duality in restricted location models.
Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, Econometrica) solve sharp expected-length problems for scalar Gaussian functionals, not simultaneous piecewise-affine curves.
Geyer (1994) gives fixed-tangent-cone constrained-estimator limits, the precursor rather than a solution to local moving-face inference.
Exact-pair searches found no all-predictor population-risk band or computed minimax band-length decision for a synthetic-control risk graph.
